Hyperglycemia During periods of physiological stress, such 
as those caused by severe illness or severe infection (sepsis), hyper-
glycemia can appear even in patients with no previous history of 
diabetes. Recently, the use of intensive insulin therapy to maintain
normal blood glucose levels has resulted in a reduction of morbid-
ity and mortality for critically ill patients. Insulin therapy not only 
controls hyperglycemia seen in metabolic stress but may aﬀ ect the 
catabolic state, reduce inﬂ ammation, and improve the immune 
response.42–44 (See Chapter 22.) Th e hyperglycemia associated with

betic patients do not experience long-term complications.
Refeeding Syndrome Refeeding syndrome is a term 
used to describe several common metabolic alterations that 
may occur during nutritional repletion of starved patients.9–11
Th is syndrome has been observed in the surviving victims of 
famine since the beginning of medical history. With the advent 
of parenteral nutrition, refeeding syndrome gained attention
because of its often dramatic and sometimes fatal presentation.
